questions.prompt: When was the last Christmas parade held?
questions.passage: As usual the annual Christmas parade was held in November this year.
questions.markingGuide: Accept 'November' (or 'November this year') — directly stated as when it was held 'as usual'. Reject other months or vague answers with no month named.

questions.prompt: In which par! of the day did the earthquake strike?
questions.passage: The buildings cast long shadows over the streets and the shopkeepers were closing up for the day when the earthquake struck.
questions.markingGuide: Accept 'late afternoon', 'evening', or 'end of the day' — inferred from long shadows and shopkeepers closing up. Reject 'morning'/'midday', or a vague 'day' that doesn't specify which part of the day.

questions.prompt: What part of the day was it?
questions.passage: Alice looked out onto the darkening streets and longed to join the rush of people heading for home.
questions.markingGuide: Accept 'evening' or 'night(time)' — 'darkening streets' and people heading home from work/school signal dusk. Reject 'morning' or 'midday'.

questions.passage: They snarled and showed their teeth as they approached each other. There was no turning back for either of them: this would decide which one would lead the pack from now on.
questions.markingGuide: Accept 'wolves' or 'dogs' (or another pack animal, e.g. wild dogs/lions) — inferred from 'pack' plus snarling and showing teeth. Reject animals that don't live in packs (e.g. cats, birds).

questions.prompt: How were they going to decide who would be the leader of the pack?
questions.passage: They snarled and showed their teeth as they approached each other. There was no turning back for either of them: this would decide which one would lead the pack from now on.
questions.markingGuide: Accept 'by fighting' (or 'whoever wins the fight/confrontation') — inferred from snarling, showing teeth and 'no turning back'. Reject answers with no reference to a fight/contest.

questions.prompt: What was the glint in the water?
questions.passage: There was a glint in the water. The bird stalled. Then, with flattened wings. It dived fifty metres into the sea.
questions.markingGuide: Accept 'a fish' (or 'fish scales flashing in the light') — the glint is what caused the bird to dive for food; accept even if phrased unconventionally (e.g. repeating 'fish/fishy'), as long as 'fish' is the identified answer. Reject 'the bird' itself (the bird is what dives, not what glints) or unrelated objects.

questions.prompt: What did the Writer think his Granny looked like?
questions.passage:
Granny lived in a dark house that was at least as old as she was. She had worn black for all of the thirty years since my grandfather had died.

Her wooden stick clumping slowly down the stairs told us that Granny was on her way. Then she was there: a dark. bent figure, her narrow, girding eyes peering at us. A pointy black hat and a broomstick would have completed the picture.

Although she looked fierce, Granny was kind. She always gave me a penny - a large, heavy coin. But, before the penny, came the question: 'How many pennies have you got now?" I counted out my penny collection from my right hand pocket.

I thought that if I didn't count out the correct number of coins I wouldn't get any more, so I never spent any of them. The number of pennies grew and so did the weight in my pocket. One day I found that some of my money had slipped through a hole. 'dreaded the thought of Granny's usual question.

Next time I saw Granny. when she asked me how many pennies I had, I gulped and stuttered.

"How many did you have?" she inquired. "How many have you got left?"

I answered the questions correctly as quickly as they were asked.

Granny smiled. "Well, you know how to do your sums." she said as she handed me a handful of pennies.
questions.markingGuide: Accept 'like a witch' or descriptions matching the text (dark, bent, fierce-looking, narrow eyes — 'a pointy black hat and a broomstick would have completed the picture'). Reject answers unrelated to her fierce/witch-like appearance.
